headline.purpose: The page's only h1: page header, auth cards, whole-page states.

title.purpose: Section and card headings, empty-state and notice titles.

body.purpose: The default for everything; running text capped at 54ch (about 70 characters).

label.purpose: Form labels, buttons, primary cells, row titles, link text.

meta.purpose: Descriptions, hints, errors, folded table meta, description-list terms; at weight 500 column headers, tabs, chips and small buttons.

caption.purpose: Badges, sidebar group labels and counts; at weight 400 timestamps, tooltips and keyboard hints.

mono.purpose: Identifiers only: SKUs, external ids, connection ids, codes, environment variable names. Platform monospace stack by deliberate exception. Never Order numbers.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Cards, sections, panels and the current sidebar item: a hairline that sharpens the lower edge.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, popovers, menus, sheets, the command palette.

shadows.name: control
shadows.purpose: Filled and outline buttons, inputs, checkboxes (Tailwind shadow-xs).

shadows.name: scroll-shade
shadows.purpose: The edge of a list that scrolls inside a popover, only where more lies beyond it.

focus.name: ring

motion.name: duration-default

narrative.overview:
The Hanza panel is the commerce admin a Shopify-fluent team trusts on sight. It does not try to be a visual world of its own: by the owner's decision it follows the category standard for commerce admins, built on shadcn/ui, and is judged against Shopify Admin. A gray canvas carries white bordered cards; a collapsible sidebar groups destinations by the job they serve; a top bar holds breadcrumbs and a command palette. Familiarity is the feature. A warehouse picker, a customer-service agent and an owner each spend whole working days here, and none of them should have to learn the furniture.

What the system does insist on is order of attention. What needs a person leads every screen: the dashboard opens with a Needs attention list instead of KPI cards, sidebar items carry counts of what waits behind them, and state is always written out in words beside a shape and a tone. Neutrals carry no hue at all; colour is reserved for links, focus and state, so that when colour appears it means something happened.

Density is that of a working tool: 14px body text, 32px controls, 44px table rows, 20px between blocks. Everything is tokenised for light and dark, and everything is translated (English and Polish), so no screen hard-codes a colour or a sentence.

The name of the North Star is provisional: it was chosen while recording the build and has not been confirmed by the owner.
keyCharacteristics: Category-standard commerce admin on shadcn/ui; quality bar Shopify Admin.
Achromatic neutrals; blue only for links, focus and selection; eight hues only for state.
One raised surface (white card, 1px border, hairline shadow) on a gray canvas.
One near-black primary action per page, top-right in the page header.
State is always tone plus icon shape plus text.
Tables follow the width of their container, not the window.
Light and dark from one token set; copy only from the message catalogues.

rules.name: The Tokens Only Rule
rules.body: Screens style with the semantic tokens and nothing else: no raw palette classes (`bg-red-500`, `text-slate-600`), no hex, no `white` or `black`. A new colour need is a new token in both themes, or it is not needed.

rules.name: The Colour Means State Rule
rules.body: Neutrals carry no hue. Blue belongs to links, focus and selection; the eight status hues belong to state. No hue is used for decoration, emphasis or branding inside the panel.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: A tone is never the only signal. It is always paired with an icon shape and with text, so a state reads in grayscale and to a screen reader.

rules.name: The Identifier Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for identifiers and nothing else: SKUs, external ids, connection ids, codes, environment variable names. They are set through the `Identifier` component (or `TextLink mono`), stay on one line in a table column, and may break anywhere in a narrow place. The face is the platform monospace stack, not a self-hosted one: a deliberate exception, because adding a production dependency needs the owner's approval and Operate mode permits system stacks.

rules.name: The Order Number Rule
rules.body: An Order number is not an identifier in this sense. People read it out and type it, so it is set in Inter with proportional figures (`orderNumberClass`, `normal-nums`). Tabular figures would widen Inter's hyphen ("fake - order - 1"), and Order numbers are read, not summed down a column.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Quantities and amounts are right-aligned in tabular figures so digits line up down a column; dates, counts and pagination summaries take tabular figures without the alignment.

rules.name: The Real Minus Rule
rules.body: A negative number is written with the typographic minus (U+2212), which is as wide as a digit in tabular figures, never with the hyphen `Intl` produces. The formatters in `src/lib/format.ts` do this; screens never format numbers or money by hand.

rules.name: The Empty Value Rule
rules.body: A value that is not there is an em dash in muted foreground with words for a screen reader (`NoValue`). Never an empty cell, never "N/A", never a bare hyphen.

rules.name: The One Primary Rule
rules.body: A page has one near-black primary button. It sits top-right in the page header, or it is the submit of a focused create or commit form. In-place saves on detail and settings pages are outline buttons everywhere, however many there are.

rules.name: The Warehouses Exception
rules.body: The Warehouses list keeps its inline two-field create form as the page's one primary, instead of a header action leading to a create page. This is deliberate: routes were not to change in this build.

rules.name: The Needs A Person First Rule
rules.body: On any screen that summarises, what waits for a person comes before totals. The dashboard opens with the Needs attention list; Orders by phase and Connection health follow, then recent activity.

rules.name: The One Surface Rule
rules.body: The card is the panel's one raised surface. Never nest two: inside a card, structure comes from hairlines, a muted fill or a toned notice.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: Everything a keyboard can reach shows the same focus ring: a 2px solid outline in Focus Blue, offset 2px. A component overrides it only to move it inside its own box, where a clipped edge would otherwise cut it off (whole-row links in a card use a -2px offset).

rules.name: The Badge Rule
rules.body: A badge is tone plus icon shape plus text. Each tone has its own shape (info: circled i; success: circled check; warning: triangle; attention: circled exclamation; critical: octagon), so a badge reads without its colour. Only a neutral tag ("Default", "Inactive") may go without an icon.

dos: Do build screens from the kit in `src/components` (`Page`, `PageHeader`, `Section`, `Panel`, `DataTable`, `FilterBar`, `Notice`, `EmptyState`, the form kit) before reaching for a primitive in `src/components/ui`.
Do give every page exactly one `<h1>` through `PageHeader` and one primary button, top-right, or as the submit of a focused create or commit form.
Do make every in-place save an outline button.
Do state every state as tone plus icon shape plus text, through `Badge` or `Notice`.
Do mark each table's primary cell, its end cell and its medium-hidden columns, and fold what a hidden column said into a `DataTableMeta` line.
Do set identifiers with `Identifier`, Order numbers with `orderNumberClass`, missing values with `NoValue`, and numbers, money and dates through the formatters.
Do take every user-facing string from `messages/en.json` and `messages/pl.json`, adding the key to both.
Do give every control an accessible name; the end-to-end flows and screen readers both find elements by role and name.
Do check every new screen in light and dark and at a narrow container width.
donts: Don't use raw palette classes, hex values, `white` or `black` in a screen.
Don't hard-code copy in a component or an action, in either language.
Don't put a second near-black button on a page. The Warehouses list's inline create form is the one recorded exception.
Don't open a summary screen with KPI cards or totals; what needs a person comes first.
Don't carry meaning by colour alone, and don't leave an icon off a badge unless it is a neutral tag.
Don't nest a card inside a card.
Don't use a hue for decoration or emphasis; colour is for links, focus and state.
Don't set anything but identifiers in monospace, and don't set Order numbers in monospace or tabular figures.
Don't write a negative number with a hyphen, or leave an empty cell where a value is missing.
Don't size layouts from the viewport where the kit uses container queries; a table or a detail page must hold with the sidebar open or collapsed.
Don't override the focus ring except to move it inside a clipped box.
Don't ship raster images. This build ships none: the only image is the vector mark `src/app/icon.svg`, which predates the rebuild.
